SU3900SE/SE Plus SU3800SE/SE Plus | High resolution Schottky SEM
Product catalog summary
Overview: The document details the specifications and features of the Hitachi High-Tech SU3900SE and SU3800SE series high-resolution Schottky Scanning Electron Microscopes (SEMs), designed for high-resolution imaging and analysis of large specimens with variable pressure capabilities.
Main Specifications:
Electron Optics: Features a ZrO/W Schottky emitter with resolutions of 0.9 nm at 30 kV and 2.5 nm at 1 kV.
Specimen Stage: 5-axis motor drive accommodating specimens up to 300 mm in diameter and 130 mm in height for SU3900SE/SE Plus.
Detectors: Includes secondary electron detector (SED), 4+1-segment semiconductor backscattered electron detector (BSED), and optional ultra variable-pressure detector (UVD).
Utility Requirements: Operates at 15 to 25°C with humidity of 60% or less, requiring AC100-115 V power supply.
Features:
High Resolution Imaging: Enhanced Schottky optics for improved top-surface imaging, especially at low accelerating voltages.
Automation and Usability: Includes guided specimen exchange, auto alignment, and EM Flow Creator for workflow automation.
Versatile Imaging Capabilities: Supports various detectors for diverse observation needs, including high-sensitivity BSED and UVD for topographic information.
Specimen Handling: Large specimen chamber supports up to 5 kg, with features like Wide Area Camera Navi and Chamber Scope for improved handling and safety.
Applications:
Semiconductor Devices: Automatic wide-area observation and uniform analysis from preprocessing to observation.
Cleanliness Control: EDS particle analysis for detecting foreign matter in manufacturing processes, compliant with ISO 16232 standards.
Conclusion: The SU3900SE and SU3800SE series SEMs offer advanced imaging capabilities, robust specimen handling, and automation features, suitable for a wide range of analytical requirements in scientific and industrial applications.
Particle Analysis and Material Composition:
Specifications: Detailed analysis of particles and alloys, including titanium oxide, Fe alloys, Cu alloys, and non-ferrous alloys, categorized by size and composition.
Procedures: Particle size distribution measured across different scales, from less than 5 µm to over 3000 µm, with data on the number of particles in each category.
Applications: Includes lithium-ion battery components, such as cathode materials and separators, and analysis of carbon nanotubes and fuel-cell catalyst particles.
Inorganic Materials: Analysis includes tungsten disulfide particles, iron particles, zinc oxide particles, high-entropy carbide films, and gallium nitride substrates, describing morphology and distribution.
Key Observations:
Titanium oxide particles are visible.
Fine pores in lithium-ion battery separators are noted.
Crystal contrast in cathode materials and platinum particles in catalysts are highlighted.
Stacked plate-like tungsten disulfide particles and fine zinc oxide particles are observed.
High-entropy carbide films show varied particle compositions and shapes.
Gallium nitride substrates reveal threading dislocations using CL signal.
Conclusion: Comprehensive data on particle size distribution and material composition, with applications in battery technology and catalyst development, emphasizing the importance of particle morphology and distribution in various industrial applications.

Uniform Analysis from Preprocessing to Observation

Here, we show an example of automatic image capture using EM Flow Creator which is described later.
